goat.name: Goat
goat.description: Goat Format is the first GX era format and one of the most popular retro Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG formats. The latest core sets are Flaming Eternity (FET) and The Lost Millennium (TLM). Notable additions include Rescue Cat, Brain Control, and Lightning Vortex. Confiscation and The Forceful Sentry are now Forbidden, while Delinquent Duo and Graceful Charity are unbanned. The format’s name comes from the historically successful Goat Control deck, however, the modern metagame revolves around Chaos Turbo. The format is simple and interactive, requiring players to use skills such as reading, bluffing, and resource management.

edison.name: Edison
edison.description: Edison is a 5D’s era format and one of the most popular retro Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG formats, backed by strong community support. Since Lightsworn Format, only Starlight Road was introduced.  The format’s name comes from the 75th Shonen Jump Championship held in Edison, New Jersey, which was won by Jeff Jones’s iconic Quickdraw Plant deck. The modern metagame is dominated by Blackwing, HERO, and Frog variants, with other decks and engines such as Dragon, Fairy, Lightsworn, Machina, Plant, and Zombie being competitive. Edison is well known for its open-ended deck-building and highly diverse metagame.

hat.name: HAT
hat.description: HAT Format is the final Zexal era format and one of the more popular retro Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG formats, backed by strong community support. The format’s name comes from the Hand, Artifact, and Traptrix engines. Since Vegas Format, Dragons of Legend (DRLG) and Primal Origin (PRIO) were introduced. Notable additions include Traptrix Dionaea, Soul Charge, Sylvan support, and the Artifact and Hand archetypes. The modern metagame features diverse decks including Artifact Traptrix, Bujin, Geargia, Mermail, and Spellbook. This was the last format before Pendulum Monsters and the removal of First Turn Draw.
